title: Wrexham warn supporters over homophobic chanting before Chelsea FA Cup tie
content:
Wrexham have warned supporters engaging in homophobic chanting during Saturday’s FA Cup tie against Chelsea will face “serious consequences”.

Wrexham released a statement on Wednesday reminding fans the “rent boy” chant often aimed at Chelsea’s current and former players is a homophobic slur and constitutes a hate crime.

The club stated any supporters found engaging in such discriminatory behaviour would risk being ejected from the SToK Cae Ras, receiving a football banning order and facing criminal charges.

Wrexham added that under the club’s regulations, this offence carries an automatic three-year ban.

“We are aware that the highly offensive and inappropriate chant of “rent boys” has been heard at Chelsea fixtures in recent years and would like to take this opportunity to reiterate our zero-tolerance approach to discriminatory behaviour,” the club statement read.

“’Rent boy’ is a homophobic slur and use of such language is a hate crime, as confirmed by the Football Association and Crown Prosecution Service. It has no place at the STōK Cae Ras or any football stadium, and anybody found using such language will face serious consequences.”

The statement continued: “North Wales Police have confirmed they will seek arrests and criminal charges.”

The Crown Prosecution Service confirmed in 2022 that it considered the term “rent boy” a homophobic slur and therefore a hate crime.

In January 2023, the Football Association added homophobic chanting to its list of rule breaches and said it can pursue action against clubs whose supporters use them at matches.

A number of clubs have issued similar statements warning supporters against the use of discriminatory language before playing Chelsea in recent seasons, including Manchester United and Leeds United.

The fixture against Chelsea will mark Wrexham’s first appearance in the FA Cup fifth round since 1997.
